correctness.summary: One-sided perturbations of any cyclic quadrilateral force exact separable invariance. An explicit cyclic kite realizes every midpoint pair and reduces that invariance to the midpoint Jensen equation, hence to affine functions under continuity. A concrete noncyclic quadrilateral fixes the slope sign, while Lambert's theorem supplies the converse.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical Japanese-theorem invariance, Lambert's linear mean-inradius criterion, diagonal-weighted nonlinear inradius identities for cyclic quadrilaterals, generalized Delaunay functional frameworks, and arbitrary increasing circumradius transforms were excluded. No located source states the affine classification for unweighted separable inradius transforms or the resulting near-cyclic power counterexamples. Lambert 1994 remains the main inaccessible full-text risk.

value.summary: The result classifies an entire natural objective family rather than adding one more Delaunay criterion, explains why the linear inradius criterion is exceptional, and gives explicit counterexamples for every nonlinear power r^p.

limitations: Continuity of the scalar transform is assumed.
Only ordinary Euclidean planar triangulations of finite point sets are treated.
No constrained, weighted, surface, or higher-dimensional extension is claimed.
The full text of Lambert's 1994 proceedings paper was not directly inspected; its abstract and multiple later summaries were checked.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; equivalent folklore in Japanese-theorem or mesh-quality literature remains possible.
